To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

Nck/Docks mediate the guidance of R-cell growth cones by controlling their actin cytoskeletal organization and that the SH3 domains of Nck/Dock are critical for the recruitment of the actin-binding protein enabled to the growth cone and that enabled is a critical regulator of actin dynamics in the growth cone.
(1) Nck/Dock and Dock3 are required for the growth cone motility of R cells, and (2) Dock3 and the SH2 domain of Dock3 play a key role in the regulation of the actin dynamics of growth cones.
the Nck/DH5/Dock180 signaling pathway plays a critical role in R cell axon guidance and that this pathway is required for R cell axon targeting and target recognition.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the mechanisms underlying axon guidance and synapse formation in the Drosophilavisual system, with the goal of understanding how the growth cone integrates and transduces extracellular cues to control the growth and navigation of the neuronal process.
understanding the mechanisms by which the actin cytokeleton is regulated in growth-cone motile processes and how the actin cyoskeleton in turn regulates the signaling systems in the growth cone.
the molecular basis for neuronal growth cone motility.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Nck/Docks are essential components of the growth-cone signaling pathways for axon guidance and targeting.
Nck/Docks are key signaling molecules in linking receptor signaling to the cytoskeleton for the guidance of R cell axons.
Nck/Docks are essential for growth cone guidance and target recognition.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Nck/Docks are key components in the receptor signaling pathways that control the remodeling of the cytoskeleton in the growth cone for directed axon growth.
Nck/Docks function as a molecular switch in the R-cell growth cones by integrating the guidance cues from the cell surface to the cytoskeleton.
Nck/Docks are the key signaling molecules in linking cell surface receptors to actin cytoskeletal dynamics for controlling growth-cone guidance in the visual system.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the R-cell growth cone contains a complex signaling network for the integration of multiple guidance cues.
the Nck/Docking complex is a key signaling hub for integrating diverse receptor signaling in controlling growth-cones behavior.

Nck/Docks can be recruited to the receptor complexes by multiple mechanisms, which in turn activate distinct downstream effectors to control different aspects of the cytoskeletal rearrangements in growth-cone motile responses.
